transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/Time: 2025-11-03 14:00 PT
- Duration: ~42 minutes
- Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Kapoor (Redwood SE), Dr. Maria Ortega (CTO, NovaCare), Liam Patel (Lead Platform Eng), Sasha Raymond (Security)

Auto-summary (auto-gen, may be noisy): Quick demo of rate limits + org/project keys in Console, brief walkthrough of API and Optimize suggestions for batching. Customer wants per-tenant quotas + clear audit trails.

[00:00] Alex Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time. I'm Alex, I'm the AE on this account and with me is Priya from our solutions engineering team. How's things on your side?
[00:10] Dr. Maria Ortega: Hey Alex, good thanks. We are, yep, eager to see how you handle multi-tenant controls. We have a bunch of internal teams and also partners pushing against our APIs; quotas matter a lot.
[00:20] Liam Patel: Quick intro: our stack is Kubernetes on EKS, we use Vault for secrets and KMS for keys, and our current vendor has had some noisy neighbors and hard-to-tune burst limits.
[00:30] Priya Kapoor: Great, thanks. Today we'll walk the Console flow for org/project keys, then show API examples for applying per-key rate limits and quotas, and finally cover telemetry/alerts. We'll also touch on dedicated vs hosted for predictable throughput.
[00:45] Sasha Raymond: We'll want to know about audit logs, SSO integration, and encryption at rest with customer-managed keys.
[00:52] Alex Chen: Absolutely. Quick ask: what are your peak QPS numbers and token/sec expectations so Priya can point to the right configs?
[01:02] Liam Patel: Right now our peak is about 250 requests/sec to LLM endpoints, average 40k tokens/min, and spikes to 600 requests/sec during batch jobs. We'll send exact logs after.
[01:15] Priya Kapoor: Perfect, that helps. Ok I'm going to share my screen — showing the Redwood Console. Note: sometimes our internal auto-captioning calls Redwood “red wood” or “read wood” in transcripts, sorry for typos in the notes.
[01:30] [screen share noise]
[01:35] Priya Kapoor: On the left nav you'll see Org -> Projects -> Keys. Here is a sample org project called "platform-prod". Each project can have multiple API keys; keys can be scoped to env, team, or partner. We support both org-level keys and project-level keys.
[01:55] Priya Kapoor: You can create per-key rate limits: requests per minute, tokens per minute, and concurrent calls. There's also a burst window that allows short bursts above the steady limit. The burst behavior is configurable — you can choose to throttle or queue based on SLO.
[02:15] Dr. Maria Ortega: And is that enforced at the edge or at the runtime? We need guarantees that noisy tenants can't affect others.
[02:25] Priya Kapoor: Good question. For hosted mode we enforce limits at the gateway layer and route to isolated runtime pools when configured. For Dedicated you get reserved GPU pools per customer which drastically reduces cross-tenant interference.
[02:40] Liam Patel: If we do Dedicated, can we still have multiple projects inside the org and different quotas per project?
[02:48] Priya Kapoor: Yes — Dedicated still uses the org/project abstraction. You can set project-level committed capacity and also per-project burst limits. It's common to have a baseline commit and allow bursts up to X for safe handling.
[03:00] [03:00] Alex Chen: We also support token-based throttles per route, so you can set lower limits for expensive generation routes and higher for embeddings or simple prompts.
[03:12] Sasha Raymond: How are audit logs exposed? We need immutable logs with SAML user mapping.
[03:20] Priya Kapoor: Audit logs are exportable to S3 or your SIEM, and every call includes the key ID, project, and user metadata if you pass the X-User header. We integrate with SAML/SSO for admin actions and RBAC, and you can enable customer-managed KMS for encryption at rest.
[03:38] Dr. Maria Ortega: You said X-User — can we inject our internal user id for attribution?
[03:42] Priya Kapoor: Yes, the API supports passing a user_id or session_id field; it's recorded in audit trails.
[03:48] [05:02] Alex Chen: A note on terminology — our "org keys" used in the product may appear as "oar keys" in some captions because of ASR errors, so ignore small typos in auto-notes.
[05:12] Priya Kapoor: Back to quotas — here's the policy editor. You can set allowed QPS, tokens/min, and also set fallback model variants. For example, if premium model reaches limit, requests automatically route to a smaller model to preserve availability.
[05:40] Liam Patel: That fallback routing — is it per-project or global?
[05:45] Priya Kapoor: It's configurable per-route and per-project. You can define routing policies that consider latency SLO or cost budget.
[05:55] Sasha Raymond: Any built-in alerts for when a project is approaching quota? We want Slack/email alerts and also programmatic webhooks.
[06:02] Priya Kapoor: Yes, you can set thresholds (e.g., 80% of tokens/min) and have alerts to Slack, PagerDuty, or webhooks. We also provide token-level cost breakdowns in the Console cost pane.
[06:20] [06:35] Dr. Maria Ortega: Curious about enforcement consistency across regions — we are global and need consistent quotas independent of where traffic lands.
[06:45] Priya Kapoor: For hosted we use a central control-plane for quotas, but enforcement is local at the edge with consistent replication; there can be sub-second eventual consistency during failover, but we have SLA targets. For strict consistency we recommend Dedicated with a single region or the Private deployment in your VPC.
[07:05] Liam Patel: On the Private deployment, does Redwood still manage the control plane? We need to know about network egress and auditability.
[07:12] Alex Chen: In Private you have customer-managed control plane options; networking is your responsibility, and logs stay inside your VPC. We can support air-gapped with additional package.
[07:25] [08:00] Priya Kapoor: Now demoing the API call: curl to POST /v1/generate with header Authorization: Bearer <project-key>. You can also use project-scoped keys that have a project_id baked in, or org keys that can be further scoped by header.
[08:20] Priya Kapoor: Example rate limit response when exceeded: HTTP 429 with X-RateLimit-Limit, X-RateLimit-Remaining, X-RateLimit-Reset. We also include a structured body explaining the quota and hinting which key hit it (key_id obfuscated).
[08:38] Liam Patel: Do you support token-pricing or hard token caps? We need quota enforcement by tokens not just requests.
[08:46] Priya Kapoor: Both. You can set tokens/min per-key and Redwood will account tokens used per response. This is important for long generations. We also have a per-request cost estimate header so clients can pre-check before sending large generations.
[09:00] [09:30] Alex Chen: Quick note — our Optimize product can suggest batching and cache configs to reduce token burn; we can run a profiling pass on your traffic to create batching suggestions.
[09:40] Dr. Maria Ortega: That would be helpful; our costs shot up last quarter.
[09:45] Priya Kapoor: We'll need sample logs to run Optimize analysis — that's one of the action items.
[10:00] [10:15] Customer: (inaudible) — discussion about SSO mapping and admin roles —
[10:30] Priya Kapoor: The RBAC model supports org-admin, project-admin, and reader roles. Admin actions are audited and can be limited by IP allowlist.
[10:45] Sasha Raymond: Do we get separate billing per project? We need chargebacks internally.
[10:52] Alex Chen: Yes, you can get per-project usage reports and cost attribution. You can export usage to CSV or BigQuery for downstream billing.
[11:05] Priya Kapoor: Now showing traffic shaping UI — create a policy, assign to a project key, set 1000 tokens/min, 50 requests/min, burst 200 requests for 30 seconds. You can also set a backoff strategy: reject vs queue vs degrade-to-smaller-model.
[11:30] Liam Patel: For queueing, what's max wait time? We prefer quick failures rather than long hangs for latency-sensitive routes.
[11:38] Priya Kapoor: Configurable; by default for interactive routes we recommend reject with informative 429s. For batch jobs you can set a queuing policy with max wait 60s.
[11:50] [12:10] Dr. Maria Ortega: How easy is it to rotate keys programmatically?
[12:15] Priya Kapoor: We have APIs to rotate keys; recommended workflow is to create new key, switch clients, then deprecate old key. We also support short-lived session tokens for ephemeral use.
[12:30] Alex Chen: Mentioning some miscaptured names in older transcripts — e.g., KV cache becomes "K-V cash" in ASR, ignore those.
[12:45] [13:00] Priya Kapoor: Demoing logs export: you can set a sink to an S3 bucket or to Kinesis/Firehose, or push to your SIEM. Each event includes timestamp, project_id, key_id (hashed), user metadata, model used, tokens_in, tokens_out.
[13:25] Liam Patel: Are token counts guaranteed accurate? We use them for billing.
[13:30] Priya Kapoor: Yes, accounting is deterministic in the runtime. For edge cases like retries we provide dedup hints.
[13:45] [15:00] Sasha Raymond: Security questions — SOC 2 scope and penetration testing cadence?
[15:10] Alex Chen: We are SOC 2 Type II; I'll share the certs and security pack. We do quarterly pen tests and can provide scoping documents.
[15:25] Sasha Raymond: Also need details on customer-managed KMS and HSM options.
[15:30] Priya Kapoor: We support BYOK via KMS and HSM integrations in Dedicated/Private modes; keys never leave your KMS. We'll add the KMS integration doc to the follow-up.
[15:45] [16:10] Dr. Maria Ortega: On pricing — how are rate limits billed? Is there a surcharge for high burst?
[16:20] Alex Chen: Billing is primarily token-based for hosted. For Dedicated you sign a commit for capacity and we bill committed plus overages. Bursts are handled by reserved burst capacity or on-demand surge which has different pricing; we'll send a sheet with examples.
[16:40] Priya Kapoor: Also note you can set spend caps per-project to avoid surprise charges.
[16:50] [18:00] Priya Kapoor: Quick demo of the CLI to create a project key: redwood projects create-key --project platform-prod --scopes generate,embeddings --tokens-per-minute 10000. The CLI mirrors API functionality.
[18:20] Liam Patel: For attribution, if partners call through our tenant, can we tag traffic to show partner_id?
[18:28] Priya Kapoor: Yes, you can include partner_id in headers which is recorded in the event.
[18:40] [20:00] Alex Chen: Summarizing tradeoffs: hosted is easiest but less absolute isolation; Dedicated gives reserved GPUs and stronger isolation; Private gives full control for regulated data with VPC and on-prem options.
[20:20] Dr. Maria Ortega: We're leaning Dedicated for now but need to validate peak handling and auditability.
[20:30] Priya Kapoor: We can run a 1-week pilot on Dedicated with a small reserved pool plus burst capacity; we'll measure latency and error rates under your workload.
[20:45] Liam Patel: We'll need detailed test plan and ramp schedule.
[20:50] Alex Chen: We'll draft a pilot plan and share within 24-48 hours.
[21:05] [22:00] Priya Kapoor: Last demo bit — Optimize suggestions: if many short requests, batching can reduce token usage by ~30% in our tests. We show per-route suggestions and config toggles.
[22:20] Dr. Maria Ortega: Nice. That could influence whether we commit to Dedicated capacity.
[22:35] [23:00] Alex Chen: Ok quick wrap. I'll list next steps and action items.
[23:10] Alex Chen: Next steps: 1) We'll send pricing and quota examples, 2) Share security pack and SOC2, 3) Draft pilot plan for Dedicated, 4) Priya to share console recording and RBAC walk-through.
[23:30] Dr. Maria Ortega: Sounds good. Also we'll send logs with exact peak numbers.
[23:38] Sasha Raymond: And we'll review the KMS/HSM doc once you send it.
[23:45] Priya Kapoor: Thanks everyone. Any final Qs?
[24:00] Liam Patel: No more from me, thanks.
[24:05] Alex Chen: Thanks, we'll follow up.

End of call.
